ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced CDD and PEP screening for all directors, UBOs, authorized signatories, and commercial counterparties against FINTRAC's published risk indicators, the Canadian Consolidated Sanctions List administered by Global Affairs Canada under the United Nations Act (S.C. 1988, c. 45) and the Special Economic Measures Act (S.C. 1992, c. 17), the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the OFAC SDN List, and additional EU/UK HM Treasury lists for maritime and cross-border banking transactions. Enhanced due diligence is required for domestic and foreign PEPs, their family members, and close associates in accordance with PCMLTFA and FINTRAC guidance; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth verification, adverse media, negative news, and probusiness sanctions ownership checks must be completed before filing with the Quebec registry or opening any escrow or installment LC facility. Continuous transaction monitoring and suspicious transaction reporting obligations apply under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Federal: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre and Novel Name Research System (NUANS) portal, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada; Provincial: Registraire des entreprises, Gouvernement du Quebec, online services and Quebec search portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11, and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, every enterprise name in Quebec must be in French; corporate names must be in Latin script and transliterated into French or English as appropriate, with the French form serving as the legal name. Federal corporate names may be in English, French, or a transliterated bilingual form, but any name using non-Latin characters must be romanized. The name must not be likely to mislead, must be distinctive, and must not falsely suggest a connection with any government, chartered body, regulated profession, or registered entity.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On name rejection, the registry issues a written refusal citing the conflicting name or statutory ground. The applicant may submit a reconsideration within 30 days through the relevant registry portal, including a revised proposed name and updated NUANS report, or request an extension of an existing reservation beyond the initial 90-day window before incorporation. For reserves and rejections under the Quebec Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, an administrative review may be pursued before the Tribunal administratif du Quebec within the statutory time limits; for federal decisions under the Canada Business Corporations Act, judicial review may be applied for in the Federal Court. Prior ministerial approval is required for any protected or sensitive token and for any proposed name suggesting regulated activity; approval letters must be obtained before filing a new name reservation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mail-drop address is not an acceptable sole demonstration of registered office or commercial substance for an ISIC 3011 commercial shipyard. Quebec and federal corporate statutes require a real registered office address accessible as the corporate seat, and Quebec registration requires an actual address in Quebec for service of process. For a shipbuilding enterprise, the registered office must coincide with physical place of business, facility, equipment asset coverage, workforce employment records, environmental permits, and ongoing yard operations. Virtual office use is limited to auxiliary correspondence and cannot satisfy CRA or Revenu Quebec permanent establishment indicators, maritime lender site inspections, Transport Canada licensing, or classification society audits.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High – quantified unannounced on-site inspection risk is 75% within the first 24 months of registration for a commercial container vessel shipyard, increasing to 90% where the entity claims QST/GST input credits, attracts bank escrow financing, or obtains marine insurance. Likely inspectors include Canada Revenue Agency, Revenu Quebec, Transport Canada Marine Safety, provincial environmental officers, municipal zoning authorities, marine lenders, underwriters, and administrative tribunals.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c. S-31.1, Part II (Incorporation and Organization, ss. 4-39) and s. 6 (registered office); Part IV (Directors and Officers).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – Direction de l’immatriculation
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Statuts constitutifs) filed electronically under the QBCA
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; no escrow account is required in Quebec for a standard business corporation. The incorporators may subscribe shares at no-par value, and a nominal stated capital deposit (e.g. CAD 1,000) is placed in a corporate bank account after the certificate of incorporation is issued.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the corporation accepts the subscriptions of the incorporators for 100,000 common shares, no par value, at a price of CAD 0.01 per share, for an aggregate paid-in capital of CAD 1,000, such funds placed in the corporate bank account; RESOLVED: That the registered office of the corporation is hereby fixed at [Address], Quebec, in accordance with section 6 of the Quebec Business Corporations Act, and the officers are directed to file any notice of change; RESOLVED: That [Name] is appointed President/CEO, [Name] is appointed Secretary-Treasurer, and [Name] is appointed acting CFO, each to serve until their successors are duly appointed; RESOLVED: That the officers are empowered to open bank accounts, execute licensing applications, and make all ancillary filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – Online Name Search and Reservation Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name research request in the REQ's secure electronic portal, providing up to three proposed names. The requested names must include a legal element ('Corp.', 'Inc.'). Wait for the name attestation/report before filing articles.
required_dossiers: Completed REQ name search / reservation form
Mandate or power of attorney if filing by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused or flagged due to conflict, file a revised name research request with alternative names; if refusal is based on distinctiveness, submit supporting evidence or appeal for reconsideration through REQ.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – Incorporation Service / REQ e-System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the name attestation, complete and submit the QBCA Articles of Incorporation via REQ's electronic platform. Pay the filing fee and upload all supporting documents; upon approval, REQ will issue a Certificate of Incorporation confirming the existence of the corporation.
required_dossiers: Registered office address (lease or landlord consent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a notice of deficiency is issued, submit corrected articles and proof of amended information within 15 calendar days; if the application is rejected on legal grounds, file a judicial review application before the Quebec Superior Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of Directors and Registered Office with REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – Declaration and Registry Update Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the certificate of incorporation is issued, file the initial declaration ('Declaration d'information') within 30 days, providing the exact registered office and the names and addresses of directors. This is a legal condition precedent for the issue of a certificate; the operating name may be registered in the same online session.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the declaration is incomplete or rejected, correct it via the REQ electronic correction portal. Quebec allows a one-time reprieve for unintentional late declarations; otherwise, apply under the Act for rectification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolution and Adoption of By-Laws
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation (acting with the corporate secretary)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board of directors meeting, adopt by-law No. 1, pass the pro-forma board resolution covering share subscriptions and registered office, and appoint the President, Secretary-Treasurer, and CFO. A consent resolution signed by all directors is permissible in writing under the QBCA.
required_dossiers: Signed unanimous board consent or minutes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any appointed director resigns or is ineligible, appoint a replacement by board resolution; if the resolution is incomplete, correct it at a subsequent board meeting or by unanimous written consent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Deposit and Corporate Bank/Escrow Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Schedule I Canadian bank or Quebec credit union authorized to operate in Quebec; escrow agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the certificate of incorporation, by-laws, resolution, and officer/director identity documents to a financial institution to open a corporate operating bank account and a segregated escrow or maritime LC facility. Deposit the agreed-paid capital and hold any customer installment payments or letters of credit in escrow.
required_dossiers: Extract from REQ (proof of legal existence and directors)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional KYC, provide audited source-of-funds and updated REQ extract; if the bank refuses, open the account at a financial institution that accepts medium-risk maritime clients or obtain a regulatory 'alternate arrangements' file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Licensing and Occupational Permits for Shipyard Operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit applications for environmental authorization (Certificat d'autorisation), occupational health and safety clearances, and municipal fire/occupancy permits for the shipyard facility. Include the site-specific environmental impact assessment/registration and a project description of the dry dock, blasting/painting areas, and waste handling systems.
required_dossiers: Site layout and structural engineer's report for dry dock/slipway
CNESST employer registration and emergency response plan
Fire safety inspection request and insurance certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is returned for completeness, respond within the specified cure period (max 45 days); if an environmental permit is refused, file an administrative review with the MELCCFP or an appeal to the Administrative Tribunal of Quebec (TAQ) within 30 days of the decision.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie (MEIE) – Direction du développement industriel et des permis
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Certificate of Authorization for Industrial Establishment (Certificat d'autorisation) under the Quebec Environment Quality Act, CQLR c. Q-2, together with a Shipyard Operating/Manufacturing Permit issued by MEIE.

environmental_impact_assessment.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) – Direction des évaluations environnementales
environmental_impact_assessment.classification_tier: Category II – Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) Registration with impact study required for new or enlarged shipyards; full EIA and ministerial approval required where project footprint exceeds 1 ha, modifies riparian areas, or includes active dry-dock berths for vessels over 30 m. Smaller repair-only operations may fall under the 'Registration' regime.
environmental_impact_assessment.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Process wastewater must comply with the Quebec Regulation respecting industrial effluents and wastewater (CQLR Q-2, r. 22): pH 6.0–9.5, BOD5 ≤ 30 mg/L, suspended solids ≤ 30 mg/L, oil and grease ≤ 15 mg/L. Emissions must meet the Regulation respecting air purification (Q-2, r. 4.1): VOC concentrations ≤ 20 mg/m3 at painting/blasting vents; hazardous/anti-fouling paints, solvents, and waste sand must be stored and disposed of under the Hazardous Waste Regulation (Q-2, r. 29).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the municipal fire inspectorate under the Quebec Fire Safety Act; structural load inspection signed by an engineer for dry docks, slipways, cranes, and dockyard structures; workplace safety clearance from CNESST under the Act respecting occupational health and safety (CQLR c. S-2.1), including dust/noise monitoring and confined space protocols.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) for federal income tax and GST/HST, portal: canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html; Revenu Québec (RQ) for Quebec corporate tax and Quebec Sales Tax (QST), portal: www.revenuquebec.ca/en/businesses/
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign shipbuilding entity must first obtain a federal Business Number (BN) from CRA by submitting Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) or registering online via 'Represent a Client'; the 9-digit BN with program accounts (e.g., RC0001 income tax, RT0001 GST/HST, RM0001 payroll, RP0001 customs) constitutes the statutory TIN. Concurrently, the entity must incorporate federally under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA) or provincially under the Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA), or complete extra-provincial registration, with a registered office in Quebec and a Canadian resident director or authorized representative, then register with Revenu Québec through the 'clients' portal (Form LM-1) to obtain the Quebec registration number and QST account. No minimum capital is required; the process is completed before the first taxable supply or contractual bid is executed.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Territorial_Scope: a resident Canadian business corporation is subject to federal Part I tax on worldwide income (general rate 15% after provincial abatement for 2025) plus Quebec corporate income tax at 11.5% under the Taxation Act (Quebec) where a permanent establishment exists in Quebec; a non-resident-owned shipyard carrying on business in Canada is taxable on Canadian-source income and is not a pass-through entity. The corporation is not eligible for US-style check-the-box classification; capital cost allowance (CCA), scientific research and experimental development (SR&ED) credits, and qualified shipbuilding investment tax credits are available.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Available elections include: (i) ITA s. 85 rollover election on qualifying property transfers (Form T2057); (ii) ITA s. 216 election for a non-resident to compute Canadian property income on a net basis; (iii) GST/HST closely related corporation election to treat certain supplies as nil consideration (Form RC4616); (iv) GST/HST Quick Method election (Form GST74) for small registrants; (v) Canada's hybrid mismatch rules (ITA s. 12.7, 18.6, 80.01(8)) override treaty benefits for deduction/non-inclusion or double-deduction outcomes, with no elective carve-out; (vi) for a foreign parent, an election under the Canada-Quebec harmonized administration agreement to align federal and provincial tax characterization, and submission of a treaty-based waiver or reduction of Part XIII withholding on dividends.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) plus QST (Quebec Sales Tax), a separate value-added tax administered by Revenu Québec in parallel to the federal GST
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in annual worldwide taxable supplies (GST/HST under Excise Tax Act s. 240; QST under QSTA s. 33); a non-resident shipyard making taxable supplies in Canada or Quebec must register once the threshold is exceeded unless a small supplier; exporters of zero-rated commercial vessels may register voluntarily to claim input tax credits (ITCs); registration is mandatory where the shipyard is engaged in a commercial activity in Canada and annual revenue exceeds CAD 30,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not impose a real-time fiscal clearance, API-based pre-approval, or digital stamping mandate at the federal level; however, CRA requires electronic record retention under ITA s. 230(4.1) and GST/HST records for six years. The Pan-Canadian e-invoice standard (Peppol BIS / EN 16931) is endorsed by CRA and GS1 Canada as the voluntary national B2B interoperability framework; Revenu Québec mandates electronic filing of QST returns and remittances through its online 'clients' service. A shipyard must issue compliant GST/QST invoices containing its BN and QST registration number, vessel description, and zero-rating status, and retain a fiscal digital record (FDR) for audit; ANSI X12 EDI or XML B2B invoices are acceptable in lieu of statutory e-invoicing.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Excise Tax Act Schedule VI: (i) a supply of a vessel used or to be used principally in the transportation of passengers or goods in international commercial trade is zero-rated under Part I, Heading 5 (including ocean container vessels and their essential shipyard equipment); (ii) a supply of goods (vessels, cranes, ship components) exported by or on behalf of the supplier is zero-rated under Part V, s. 1 where the goods are delivered outside Canada, delivered to a common carrier or customs broker for export, or exported via a marine freight forwarder with proof of export retained for two years; (iii) services provided solely for the benefit of a non-resident purchaser (ship design, engineering, outfitting, project management) are zero-rated under Part V, s. 7 where no element of the service is rendered in Canada for local consumption; (iv) the shipyard must be a GST/HST registrant and obtain a matching QST zero-rating treatment under the QSTA regulations; the builds must be destined for non-resident owners in international trade to qualify.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA Form B13A / Canadian Export Declaration or Canada Customs Invoice) evidencing export from Canada
Bill of Lading (ocean or multimodal transport document issued to the non-resident purchaser)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank foreign-exchange contract evidencing receipt of foreign currency payment
Commercial invoice (certified) with vessel hull identification number and HS code 8901.20 issued to the non-resident buyer
Carrier's certificate or freight forwarder's proof of physical movement of the vessel out of Canadian waters
GST/HST and QST zero-rated supply record: purchase contract, delivery protocol, and CRA-validated export ledger
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess within the normal four-year period, extended to seven years for misrepresentation attributable to neglect, carelessness, or willful default, and without time limit where fraud or misrepresentation is established (ITA s. 152(4); ETA s. 298(1)); a false or fraudulent export zero-rating claim triggers the ETA s. 280 penalty of CAD 250 or 25% of net tax, and the ITA s. 163(2) gross-negligence penalty of 50% of tax understated; CRA and Revenu Québec may retroactively claw back input tax credits (ITCs), deny refunds and assessment, and impose arrears interest and penalities of 50% on the amount of QST evaded when supporting export documentation is not retained for six years or where the 180-day repatriation benchmark is not met; criminal prosecution is possible under the Criminal Code for aiding false or deceptive statements in customs and export documentation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a floating exchange rate regime with unrestricted capital and current account convertibility. Resident corporations face no prior approval requirements for profit remittances, dividend distributions, or capital repatriation. FX conversions are permitted without restriction, subject solely to ongoing AML/CTF compliance and KYC obligations administered by FINTRAC.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender or conversion of export proceeds is required. Receipts may be retained in foreign currency accounts or freely converted to CAD. Exporters must report all cash transactions exceeding CAD 10,000 to FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act; no statutory conversion ratios or timelines apply.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility for offshore digital EMIs. Canadian corporations are subject to FINTRAC oversight and the Payment Services Act; offshore digital wallet or crypto platforms are restricted for resident entities and require specific licensing or exemptions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote KYC and digital onboarding is permitted through accredited providers for Canadian corporations. For high-risk sectors such as shipbuilding, directors and signatories may require in-person verification or biometric authentication at a branch.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained high cash inflows or unusual transaction patterns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Project contracts, audited financial statements, director affidavits, and source-of-funds evidence

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore ownership structures or related-party transactions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Beneficial ownership declarations, corporate charts, and transfer pricing studies

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital without matching trade documentation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Trade agreements, LC documents, and buyer correspondence

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound wires via SWIFT MT103 using purpose codes such as 'CAP' for capital contributions or 'EQU' for equity. All transactions require corporate resolutions, KYC verification, and FX documentation for audit compliance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing via SWIFT MT103 for direct payments or Commercial Letters of Credit through correspondent banks. Escrow accounts with milestone releases are standard for shipyard projects. All disbursements require supporting trade documents and full AML screening.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of the enterprise's registration date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty; after 1 year of continuous default, administrative dissolution and strike-off from the enterprise register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Corporation Income Tax Return (T2) with financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the corporation's fiscal period end; balance-due day is 2 months after year-end (3 months for eligible CCPCs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% per month up to 12 months; daily compound interest; gross-negligence penalties up to 50% of understated tax.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the corporation's fiscal period end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing and late-payment penalties with daily interest; administrative collection measures and possible tax registration suspension.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate records confirmation and shareholder meeting resolutions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered-office records (internal; subject to inspection by REQ, CRA and Revenu Québec)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At each calendar year end or within 15 months of the previous annual meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain registers may trigger civil fines under the Quebec Business Corporations Act and evidentiary prejudice in court disputes.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for reporting issuers, public corporations and corporations subject to securities legislation; private corporations may dispense with an auditor only by unanimous shareholder resolution unless a shareholder holding at least 10% of voting shares demands an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises; Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE / CPA Canada Handbook Part II) for private corporations.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The register of individuals with significant control (ISC) must be completed, maintained at the registered office and updated within 15 days of any change; an annual confirmation by directors is required at the annual meeting, and the register is available for statutory inspection by REQ, other authorities and qualifying shareholders.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC)
Minute Book with resolutions and meeting records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CAD 300 - CAD 1,200 (USD 225 - USD 900) for registered office and corporate agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: CAD 10,000 - CAD 45,000 (USD 7,500 - USD 34,000) for a commercial shipyard entity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined standard general corporate income tax rate for a Quebec corporation: 15% federal and 11.5% Quebec. A qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporation may access a federal small-business rate of 9% and, subject to Quebec eligibility rules, a Quebec small-business rate of 3.2%, producing a potential combined rate of 12.2% on eligible income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Potential incentives include the federal Scientific Research and Experimental Development regime, federal investment tax credits, capital-cost allowance and accelerated investment incentive rules, Quebec research and development tax credits, Quebec investment and innovation incentives, and sector-specific shipbuilding assistance where statutory conditions are satisfied. The federal general corporate rate is reduced by a 13% abatement for income allocated to provinces. The small-business limit is generally CAD 500,000 and is reduced by associated-corporation allocation, taxable capital employed in Canada, and adjusted aggregate investment income. Eligibility must be tested separately for manufacturing, research, export, and shipbuilding activities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Canada Revenue Agency T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, including applicable schedules, filed through CRA-certified electronic filing software or CRA corporation Internet filing. Paper filing is permitted only in prescribed circumstances. Quebec income tax return CO-17 and applicable schedules are filed through Revenu Quebec's authorized electronic filing system or approved software.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual corporate income tax return; federal and Quebec instalments are generally monthly, with quarterly instalments potentially available to qualifying corporations.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The T2 and CO-17 are generally due within six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end. Any balance of tax is generally payable two months after year-end, or three months after year-end for qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporations meeting the statutory conditions. Instalments are due monthly or, where permitted, quarterly.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, business number, corporation type, tax year, fiscal period, address, province of residence, incorporation details, and electronic filing authorization.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation carrying on business in Canada must identify its Canadian permanent establishment, Canadian business number, fiscal period, and taxable Canadian presence. Treaty-protected entities should disclose the relevant treaty position and retain supporting records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related and associated corporations, ownership, control, associated-corporation allocation, and small-business limit allocation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report foreign parent, sister, subsidiary, and commonly controlled entities where required. Association and control must be assessed under Canadian tax rules, not solely under local corporate-law ownership percentages.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of accounting net income or loss to income for tax purposes, including non-deductible expenses, timing adjustments, reserves, depreciation, provisions, and foreign-exchange items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude accounting income not attributable to the Canadian permanent establishment and allocate expenses using a defensible factual basis. Do not deduct head-office charges, interest, royalties, or management fees without transfer-pricing and benefit evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital cost allowance, undepreciated capital cost balances, additions, dispositions, recapture, terminal losses, and available accelerated deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only depreciable property used to earn income in Canada or otherwise allocated to the Canadian business. Maintain asset-level records for vessels, cranes, dry docks, fabrication equipment, tooling, and leasehold improvements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Summary of specified foreign property and foreign investment income where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Canadian-resident corporations must assess foreign affiliate reporting, foreign accrual property income, foreign tax credits, and Form T1134 obligations. A non-resident corporation generally reports only its Canadian taxable activities but may have separate information-reporting obligations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 20 and Schedule 31 or applicable investment-tax-credit schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Scientific research and experimental development expenditures and investment tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only qualifying Canadian expenditures incurred for eligible experimental development. Engineering design, production optimization, welding trials, corrosion testing, and prototype work require contemporaneous technical narratives and project-level cost records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal foreign income tax credits and related foreign-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report foreign income, legally imposed foreign tax, source-country details, and limitation calculations. Treaty relief and foreign tax credit claims cannot exceed the applicable Canadian limitation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Shareholder, ownership, control, and associated-corporation information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose non-resident shareholders and relevant ownership chains. Beneficial ownership, nominee arrangements, and control rights must be documented consistently with corporate registers and anti-money-laundering records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 23 or applicable loss schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-capital losses, net capital losses, restricted losses, utilization, carryback, and carryforward balances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-capital losses are generally carried back three taxation years and forward twenty taxation years. Net capital losses are generally carried back three years and forward indefinitely. Acquisition-of-control rules may restrict losses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: CO-17 Quebec Corporation Income Tax Return
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec taxable income, Quebec allocation, capital tax-related information where applicable, Quebec credits, instalments, and balance payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File where the corporation carries on business in Quebec or has Quebec taxable income. Allocate income and remuneration using federal and Quebec allocation rules and reconcile Quebec filings with the T2.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 5 and Quebec credit schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable dividends, dividend tax credits, refundable taxes, Quebec refundable and non-refundable credits, and other tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not claim Canadian-resident dividend treatment for amounts paid to non-resident shareholders. Withhold and remit non-resident tax separately through the CRA payer account.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 23, T106, T1134, T1135, and Country-by-Country Reporting forms where applicable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign affiliate, foreign-property, non-arm's-length transaction, and multinational-group information reporting.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: T106 generally applies to Canadian taxpayers with reportable non-arm's-length non-resident transactions exceeding the statutory threshold. T1134 applies to foreign affiliates of Canadian residents. T1135 generally applies to Canadian-resident corporations holding specified foreign property exceeding CAD 100,000. Country-by-country reporting generally applies to qualifying multinational enterprise groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: For a late T2 return with a balance owing, the federal penalty is generally 5% of the unpaid balance plus 1% for each complete month late, up to 12 months. A repeated late-filing penalty can generally be 10% of the unpaid balance plus 2% for each complete month late, up to 20%. False statements or omissions may attract a penalty of 50% of the understated tax or overstated credit, subject to statutory rules. Interest compounds daily at prescribed rates. Quebec applies separate late-filing, instalment, interest, and administrative penalties. Failure to file required information returns can generate additional fixed or transaction-based penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Canadian withholding tax on taxable dividends paid or credited to a non-resident, subject to treaty reduction. Under the Canada-United States treaty, the rate is generally 5% for a qualifying corporate beneficial owner holding at least 10% of the voting power and 15% in other cases. Other treaties commonly reduce the rate to 5%, 10%, or 15%, depending on ownership and treaty conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Canadian payer must establish the beneficial owner's identity, residence, entitlement to treaty benefits, and applicable ownership facts before applying a reduced rate. Obtain a valid certificate of residence or equivalent reliable evidence from the recipient and retain ownership, legal-entity, and beneficial-ownership records. Use CRA Form NR301 for treaty representations by an individual or qualifying entity, NR302 for partnerships, and NR303 for hybrid entities where applicable. If evidence is incomplete, withhold at 25% and allow the recipient to seek a refund. Remit withholding to the CRA by the 15th day of the month following payment or credit, file the applicable NR4 information return by the last day of March following the calendar year, and issue NR4 slips. Treaty anti-abuse, limitation-on-benefits, principal-purpose, beneficial-ownership, and conduit restrictions must be reviewed.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The domestic Canadian rate is generally 25% on royalties and interest paid or credited to a non-resident, subject to statutory exemptions and treaty relief. Treaty royalty rates commonly range from 0% to 10%; patent, know-how, copyright, and equipment-use classifications must be analyzed under the applicable treaty. Treaty interest rates commonly range from 0% to 15%, with many treaties using 10% or exempting arm's-length interest. The Canada-United States treaty commonly provides a 0% rate for qualifying arm's-length interest and a 10% royalty rate, subject to treaty definitions and conditions. Related-party interest must satisfy thin-capitalization rules, transfer-pricing rules, debt-equity characterization, and withholding obligations. Quebec generally does not impose a separate provincial withholding tax on ordinary dividends, royalties, or interest paid to non-residents, but Quebec income-tax allocation and information obligations may remain.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 aggregate value of non-arm's-length non-resident transactions generally triggers Form T106 reporting and contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation requirements. Canadian law does not impose a separate OECD-style mandatory Master File and Local File filing package for every taxpayer; documentation must nevertheless support the arm's-length nature of material transactions. Country-by-country reporting generally applies to a constituent entity of a qualifying multinational enterprise group with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million in the preceding fiscal year.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada has no standalone economic-substance regulation equivalent to the United Kingdom, Cayman Islands, or certain other jurisdictions. Substance is relevant through the general anti-avoidance rule, treaty anti-abuse rules, beneficial-ownership requirements, sham and characterization doctrines, transfer-pricing analysis, thin-capitalization provisions, foreign-affiliate rules, and principal-purpose tests. A Quebec shipyard should maintain real Canadian management, employees, production assets, procurement functions, technical decision-making, inventory and project controls, banking records, and risk-bearing capacity proportionate to the profits claimed in Quebec. Intercompany procurement, design, engineering, financing, warranty, licensing, and management charges require written agreements and evidence of actual services and benefits.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.shipyard_specific_transfer_pricing_contr: Apply transaction-level analysis to vessel construction contracts, progress-billing arrangements, customer deposits, maritime installment letters of credit, escrow accounts, steel and equipment procurement, subcontracting, design and engineering services, vessel warranties, intellectual property, financing, guarantees, insurance, and foreign-group management charges. Revenue recognition for long-term contracts must be reconciled between financial reporting and tax reporting. Customer advances and escrow balances must not be treated as unrestricted profit. Customs valuation, GST/QST, permanent-establishment allocation, and income-tax transfer pricing should use consistent facts while applying their distinct statutory tests.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate tax evasion and false tax reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing shipyard revenue, fabricating subcontractor costs, circular invoicing, understating vessel contract margins, claiming non-qualifying SR&ED expenditures, or knowingly filing materially false T2 or CO-17 information.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Income Tax Act, tax evasion may result in fines ranging from 50% to 200% of the tax sought to be evaded and imprisonment for up to five years. Gross-negligence penalties can generally equal 50% of the understated tax or overstated credit, in addition to tax and interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may face criminal prosecution where personal participation, authorization, knowledge, or wilful blindness is proven. Ordinary corporate income-tax debt does not automatically create personal liability, but directors may be jointly and severally liable for unremitted source deductions and certain GST/HST amounts, subject to statutory due-diligence defenses. Courts may impose restitution or fines; imprisonment is possible for criminal convictions. Travel restrictions are not an automatic tax consequence but may arise from bail, probation, enforcement, or criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to remit payroll deductions and indirect taxes
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using employee source deductions, GST/HST, or QST collected from customers as working capital; failing to register, collect, remit, or reconcile amounts; or issuing unsupported input-tax credits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The CRA and Revenu Quebec may assess the unremitted amounts, interest, gross-negligence or failure-to-remit penalties, director-liability assessments, garnishment, liens, and legal costs. Deliberate tax fraud may produce criminal fines and imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be assessed personally for certain unremitted payroll deductions and GST/HST or QST amounts if statutory conditions are met and due diligence is unavailable. A director should retain cash-flow controls, remittance calendars, reconciliations, approval evidence, and documented corrective action.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging unsupported royalties, management fees, guarantees, financing costs, procurement commissions, or engineering fees to the Quebec corporation; allocating losses to the shipyard while foreign affiliates retain routine or entrepreneurial returns; or failing to report T106 transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The CRA may reassess income under the arm's-length principle, deny deductions, impose transfer-pricing adjustment penalties generally equal to 10% of the adjustment where statutory conditions are met, assess interest, and apply the general anti-avoidance rule or treaty anti-abuse provisions. Quebec may make corresponding reassessments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors generally face corporate reassessment rather than automatic personal liability. Personal exposure can arise from participation in fraud, knowingly false records, obstruction, criminal tax evasion, or director-liability provisions applicable to source deductions and indirect taxes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Treaty abuse and improper withholding-tax reduction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Applying a reduced dividend, royalty, or interest rate without valid residence evidence; routing payments through a conduit; misrepresenting beneficial ownership; or using a treaty entity without satisfying limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose requirements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The payer may be assessed for the unwithheld tax, interest, penalties, and information-return failures. CRA may deny treaty relief, apply the domestic 25% rate, and reassess related deductions where anti-avoidance or characterization rules apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible directors and officers may be exposed for deliberate false certifications or knowing failures to remit. Personal exposure is strongest where the individual controlled the payment process, ignored clear deficiencies, or participated in concealment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company, beneficial ownership, and economic-substance failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a nominal Quebec corporation with no real employees, premises, production control, commercial risk, or decision-making while booking substantial shipbuilding profits; using nominee shareholders; or disguising the true recipient of dividends, royalties, or financing income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Potential consequences include denial of treaty benefits, income reallocation, GAAR reassessment, transfer-pricing adjustments, withholding-tax assessments, penalties, interest, corporate-register consequences, and financial-institution account restrictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil is exceptional and fact-specific. Directors may nevertheless incur direct civil or criminal liability for fraud, misrepresentation, oppressive conduct, breach of fiduciary duty, or statutory remittance failures. Civil restitution, asset preservation, and enforcement orders may be available; travel bans or imprisonment require separate judicial or criminal processes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-money-laundering, proceeds of crime, and sanctions violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained vessel deposits, using opaque escrow structures, processing funds for sanctioned counterparties, concealing beneficial owners, structuring payments to avoid reporting, or dealing with proceeds of crime.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FINTRAC administrative monetary penalties vary by violation and compliance history and may reach significant amounts, including up to CAD 1,000,000 for certain serious violations. Criminal proceeds-of-crime and money-laundering offences can result in substantial fines and imprisonment, including life imprisonment for laundering proceeds of indictable offences in the most serious cases. Sanctions violations may attract prosecution, asset seizure, and penalties under Canadian sanctions legislation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, officers, compliance personnel, and beneficial owners may be prosecuted where they knowingly participate, direct, counsel, or facilitate the conduct. Potential consequences include fines, imprisonment, forfeiture, director disqualification in appropriate proceedings, asset restraint, and court-imposed bail or travel conditions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misclassifying imported steel, engines, cranes, or vessel components; understating customs value; exporting controlled marine technology without authorization; breaching sanctions; or operating without required federal, Quebec, port, environmental, or maritime approvals.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Consequences may include reassessed duties and taxes, customs penalties, seizure, forfeiture, administrative monetary penalties, permit suspension, procurement exclusion, environmental orders, and criminal prosecution depending on the statute and conduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Corporate officers and directors may be personally prosecuted for knowing or consented violations. Civil damages, remediation costs, forfeiture, fines, and imprisonment are possible for serious or intentional conduct; ordinary corporate liability remains distinct from personal criminal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Records destruction, obstruction, and audit interference
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Destroying project ledgers, emails, engineering records, payroll files, beneficial-ownership information, or transfer-pricing studies; refusing lawful CRA or Revenu Quebec requests; or creating backdated agreements after an audit begins.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Failure-to-provide-information penalties, obstruction offences, adverse reassessments, preservation orders, prosecution, fines, and imprisonment may apply. Record-retention failures may also compromise deductions, credits, treaty relief, and loss claims.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individuals who direct, authorize, or knowingly assist obstruction may face personal criminal and civil exposure. Directors should implement litigation holds, tax-audit protocols, document retention, privilege controls, and truthful cooperation procedures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate insolvency and unlawful profit extraction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, management fees, shareholder loans, or related-party repayments while insolvent or while statutory remittances, secured creditors, employees, or shipyard completion obligations remain unpaid.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Potential consequences include dividend recovery, oppression remedies, fraudulent-preference or transfer-at-undervalue claims, insolvency proceedings, director compensation orders, tax reassessments, and creditor damages.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal liability for prohibited dividends, unpaid wages or source deductions, breach of fiduciary duty, oppression, fraudulent transfers, and transactions approved without reasonable solvency analysis. The corporate veil does not protect intentional asset stripping or statutory director breaches.
